title: When I Was Young I Could Lift That

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a young adult aged 18-25)

collection.description: An elder claims to have lifted the big stone overhead in youth, and a young adult asks to see it: give it a try, or teach instead.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: There's a big round stone near the beach that young people try to lift to show off. Watching (friend) struggle with it, (subject) remarks that when (subject.he/she) was young, (subject.he/she) used to lift it above (subject.his/her) head. Every day. For fun. (friend) puts the stone down and steps back politely. "Show me?"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) bends down, takes a good grip, and heaves. The stone rises about the width of a finger, then settles back. (subject) straightens up slowly and dusts off (subject.his/her) hands. "The sea's made it heavier," (subject.he/she) explains. "All that salt." (friend) agrees solemnly that the sea does that.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Not today," says (subject). "But you're doing it all wrong." (subject.He/she) shows (friend) how to bend the knees, keep the back straight and hug the stone close. On the next try, (friend) lifts it to (friend.his/her) chest. (subject) beams as if (subject.he/she) had lifted it (subject.him/her)self. In a way, (subject.he/she) feels (subject.he/she) did.
